chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), the cat is a predator, but there is no objection to its leftovers. And I would be embarrassed before God to leave food because a cat has eaten from it.'

key_terms.سَبُع: Sabi' — a predator or beast of prey; legally significant because predators' su'r is subject to special scrutiny in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.سُؤْر: Su'r — the leftover water or food remaining after an animal has drunk or eaten from a vessel; central to rulings on ritual purity
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali — a foundational jurisprudential compendium dictated by the Prophet (SAWW) to Imam Ali (AS), preserved across generations and frequently cited in al-Kafi
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba's — 'there is no objection/harm'; standard fiqhi expression indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is the leftover water or food of a cat ritually pure in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cites the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) — a foundational legal compendium attributed to Imam Ali, dictated to him by the Prophet — to establish that the cat, though legally classified as a predator (sabi'), does not render its leftover water or food ritually impure. The Imam reinforces this ruling with a personal expression of piety: he would feel ashamed before God to waste food merely because a cat touched it. This hadith is a cornerstone ruling in Shia fiqh on the ritual purity of cat su'r, and illustrates how the Imams cite the Book of Ali as a supreme legal authority.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said,

‘In the Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The cat is a predator, but there is no problem with its leftovers, and I<sup>asws</sup> would be embarrassed from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> if I<sup>asws</sup> were to leave food because a cat has eaten from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

it is in the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that cats are beasts but there is no offense in using the leftover of what they eat. I feel embarrassed before Allah to throw away a food from which a cat has eaten.’”
